title: Private deployments exec elevator and technical gap maps
body:
Purpose
---
Short working brief for GTM and AE teams: concise executive + technical elevators tailored to regulated workloads (finance, healthcare, public sector) and a fresh framing of competitor delta maps and buyer objections. Meant to be a compact reference for prep calls and pitch rehearsals.

Audience
---
Primary: AEs, Solutions Engineers, Sales Engineers, Strategic GTM leads. Secondary: Product marketers and SE hiring for pilot runs.

Context and constraints
---
- Customers increasingly ask for private deployments (VPC / on-prem) when data residency, auditability, or regulatory controls are showstoppers.
- We need crisp, layered messaging: 1) Executive (value/risk), 2) Technical (surface-level architecture + assurance), 3) Procurement/legal (contract and control plane guarantees).
- Competitors: managed-hosted vendors that promise simple APIs, and self-hosted inference vendors that require customers to build ops. Our sweet spot: unified API and production-grade runtime with optional private control plane and clear fallbacks.

Executive elevator (30–60s)
---
"Redwood offers enterprise-grade LLM inference that keeps your sensitive data and controls where you need them. With private VPC or on‑prem deployments we deliver the same predictable latency, cost controls, and rollout tooling you get from our hosted API — but with customer-managed networking, KMS integrations, and audit-ready logs. In short: you don’t trade developer velocity for compliance. We help you run high-throughput models with SLA-backed predictability while meeting your compliance, residency, and procurement guards."

Technical elevator (90s, for CTO/SRE/ML infra)
---
- Deployment modes: private VPC (control plane hosted by Redwood but management plane isolated to customer VPC), private control plane (customer-hosted control plane / optional on‑prem package), and air-gapped on‑prem for high-reg clients.
- Runtime: GPU-optimized inference engine with automatic KV/prefix caching, dynamic batching, and quantization profiles. Same runtime as hosted product => consistent performance profiles and simpler model pinning/rollbacks.
- Security controls: customer KMS/HSM integration, encrypted-in-transit & at-rest defaults, role-based access tied to your identity provider (OIDC/SAML), and comprehensive audit logs compatible with SIEM ingestion.
- Operational guarantees: reserved capacity options, deterministic routing policies (region/fallback model), and canary/A-B rollout controls visible in Redwood Console.

Key buyer objections and recommended rebuttals
---
1) "We need full control; we can’t trust a vendor-managed control plane."
   - Rebuttal: Offer private control plane option (customer-hosted) and an air-gapped deployment blueprint. For compliance-first deals, present our architecture diagrams, runbook, and SOC2+ attestation materials. If they want the simplest path, explain VPC-hosted control plane with strict egress rules and customer KMS so Redwood never has access to keys.
2) "How do we prove model output fidelity stays the same as hosted?"
   - Rebuttal: Emphasize same serving runtime and model binary parity. Offer to run a small eval suite (customer test prompts + Redwood’s regression harness) during POC and produce deterministic perf/quality baselines.
3) "Operational burden — who will patch, monitor, and scale?"
   - Rebuttal: For Private VPC we operate the runtime but routing and network stay in your VPC. For Private control plane/on‑prem, offer managed support retainer + runbooks + optional 24x7 war‑room support. Highlight autoscaling policies and dedicated capacity options to reduce ops overhead.
4) "We need an audit trail that ties prompts/responses to RBAC and retention policies."
   - Rebuttal: We support token-level tracing, per-route logs, retention controls, and SIEM export. We can map logs to your IAM identities (via SAML/OIDC) during pilot.

Competitive delta map (concise)
---
- Hosted-only vendors (easy integration)
  - Strengths: fastest time-to-value, simple billing.
  - Weaknesses: poor for regulated buyers (data residency, key access).
  - Redwood angle: same dev experience + private options and model pinning.

- Self-hosted runtimes / OSS stacks
  - Strengths: full control, no vendor lock-in.
  - Weaknesses: heavy ops cost, less mature batching/throughput optimizations, no SLAs.
  - Redwood angle: we provide the runtime optimizations + managed/pipeline options so customers avoid rebuilding infra while keeping controls.

- Large cloud providers with private endpoint offerings
  - Strengths: enterprise sales motion, integrated cloud controls.
  - Weaknesses: limited model catalog, coupling to cloud provider, variable latency/cost tradeoffs.
  - Redwood angle: neutral model catalog + predictable performance across clouds + flexible hardware/quantization guidance.

Tactical win themes and proof points (what to show in first 30 days)
---
- Security pack: KMS integration demo, SIEM log export sample, and network segmentation diagram.
- Performance baseline: run a 2-day head-to-head of sample workload: tokens/sec, median p95 latency, and cost-per-1000-tokens (hosted vs private).
- Compliance pack: provide SOC2 summary, on‑demand whitepaper for FedRAMP/PCI implications, and contract language snippets for data residency and audit access.
- Pilot offer: 6-week pilot with clearly scoped SLOs, 2-week knowledge transfer, and a rollback plan. Conservative pricing to remove procurement blocker.

Conversation scripts (short snippets)
---
- For CISO:
  "We can integrate with your HSM and keep all keys in your control — Redwood never sees plaintext. We'll produce an exportable audit trail so your risk team can validate requests and retention policies without exposing content."

- For CTO:
  "You get the same optimized runtime we run for our hosted customers; that means consistent throughput and predictable cost. If you want complete isolation, we can ship the control plane components to your environment or run an on-prem package with our support team."

- For Procurement/Legal:
  "We'll include clear contractual SLAs for availability and an agreed data handling appendix that defines ownership, export rights, and incident response timelines. For larger deals we accept tighter indemnity and audit clauses as part of an enterprise addendum."

Unresolved items / open asks (TODOs)
---
- Legal: finalize template contract language for customer-hosted control plane (PROC-legal-ask).
- Product: produce a 1-page diagram pack for three deployment topologies (VPC control plane, customer-hosted control plane, air-gapped on‑prem).
- Solution templates: create a turnkey pilot checklist + runbook for a 6-week trial footprint.

Customer proof stories to surface
---
- Finance customer (stealth name): reduced inference cost 35% after moving to dedicated pools; maintained audit trail for regulators.
- Healthcare pilot: validated model fidelity parity during on‑prem run and satisfied internal clinical governance review. (Need to get permission to publish)

Next steps for AE/SE
---
1) Rehearse the exec and technical elevators; practice the CISO snippet with an SE.
2) Attach the security pack and the pilot offer to initial outreach.
3) Log objections in the shared Slack channel above to help centralize rebuttal templates and legal asks.
4) If customer requests private control plane, open JIRA ticket (PROD-1423) and tag eng-privdeploy for intake.

Appendix: quick FAQ (short)
---
Q: "Do you store customer prompts/outputs?"
A: Default retention is configurable. For private deployments we can configure zero retention or local-only retention per contract.

Q: "Can we run our own models?"
A: Yes — bring-your-own-model is supported via model pinning and artifact registry. We provide guidance on quantization profiles and kernel selection.

Q: "What if we need GovCloud or sovereign region?"
A: We support region-specific deployments and can provide private control plane in approved cloud regions or on-prem packages for sovereign requirements.
